doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Return to New York in the late 1960s
title: Returning to New York in 1967 and Blue Mitchell at Smalls
summary: Ware leaves Chicago before the riot, arrives in a riot-torn New York, and plays with Blue Mitchell opposite Lucky Thompson.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, anyway, I decided to come back to New York. That was around August, around July. I left Chicago just before the riot started out there, and I got to New York, where they had another riot up there in Harlem. That's when Lindsay walked the streets, you know, (unintelligible) doing all that.

It kind of stopped the different bands from making gigs across the country. Cities were in a lot of turmoil during those times. If you were in New York, they had enough clubs and concert halls to kind of sustain a musician.

Anyway, I come to New York and the word preceded me that I was back in town. I hadn't been in New York since, like I said, '63 -- '64, when I come out of the hospital on my way back to Chicago. Anyway, I got a little gig with Blue Mitchell (PHONETIC). We played at Smugglers (PHONETIC) Paradise. It was afternoon, wasn't a cocktail set, but it was a little afternoon engagement. There was two bands. There was -- Lucky Thompson had a four-piece group and Blue Mitchell had a four-piece

group. Blue had Walter Davis, Jr., myself, Al Foster and Lucky had Victor Sproles (PHONETIC), another Chicago bassist, a friend of mine, and I think he had Bill English on drums and I forgot who his pianist was.
